why: Both wrapped the same single AsyncOpenAI client and verified all five call sites, but B actually closed the loop that decides whether anything routes at all — the shipped configs select claude-3-7-sonnet, which A itself reports leaves an unmodified deployment sending zero requests to Router and only proposes fixing, while B fixed it on a tested branch with live evidence, and also made the documented setup importable so the app starts. B's system-level judgment goes deeper and is better verified: the dead `initialize_agent` wiring (default_factory=LLM meant per-agent `[llm.<name>]` sections were read by nobody) is the find that turns per-role model choice into a config decision — the main Router lever here — and B measured Flex at exactly half price, cross-vendor fallthrough with tools, per-role provider_timeout, and cache behaviour on both vendors, where A relies on the fact sheet for Flex and left the spend-label question unmeasured.
A_best: The honesty of the trade-off writing: every item's "loses" is specific and non-defensive, and the fallback analysis is the sharpest Router detail in either report — that a models list disables allow_flex_tier, that the least capable candidate caps tools and modalities, that truncated attempts still bill, and that a mid-run model swap can be worse than a clean failure for a loop dependent on tool discipline.
B_best: Finding that `BaseAgent.initialize_agent`'s `self.llm = LLM(config_name=self.name.lower())` never executed because the field was declared with `default_factory=LLM` — so every agent shared one client and `[llm.manus]`/`[llm.data_analysis]` were dead config — then fixing it, which converts per-role model choice (a 10–40x spread from claude-opus-5 to claude-haiku-5-5) into a config edit; it also correctly disclosed that this splits the `max_input_tokens` budget per agent.
A_worst: It ships a migration that routes nothing for the configuration the project actually ships, and then calls the fix (model_map to a catalog id) a decision "a human should make" — deferring the one change that makes the other eight items apply; it also mislabels `ask_with_images` as "the vision path" the agent's eyes use, when that method has no caller in the codebase (images reach the model via `base64_image` through `ask_tool`), which weakens the premise of its own image item.
B_worst: Blast radius and scope discipline: the per-agent LLM branch quietly changes the semantics of the `max_input_tokens` safety budget from process-wide to per-agent, and bundles an unrelated f-string refactor in `data_visualization.py`; the shipped-config model change (3.7 → sonnet-5) is also a behaviour change for default deployments justified mainly on price and catalog membership, with no offline check of agent-loop quality.
